title: NASA’s Crew-12 Astronauts Splash Down After 237 Days
summary:
Four astronauts from NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission have returned to Earth after more than seven months on the International Space Station. Their spacecraft splashed down Thursday in the Pacific Ocean near Los Angeles.

The crew spent 237 days in orbit, traveled more than 100 million miles, and circled Earth more than 3,792 times. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman thanked the team and their families, saying the mission advanced science and showed the skills needed for future exploration.

The returning crew included NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev. The capsule touched down at 8:34 a.m. Pacific time. SpaceX recovery teams brought the astronauts aboard specialized ships. After medical checks, they were expected to travel to NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

Crew-12 launched on February 13 and docked with the station the next day. For Meir and Fedyaev, it was a second spaceflight. For Hathaway and Adenot, it was their first.

On the station, the astronauts spent hundreds of hours on research that could support future trips to the Moon and Mars and help people on Earth. Projects included studying stem cells in space, testing ways to make IV fluids when needed, and looking at nutrition and blood flow in microgravity.

Meir also completed four spacewalks during the mission, bringing her career total to seven. That ranks her third among NASA women for career spacewalks, behind Peggy Whitson and Suni Williams.

NASA planned a news conference at Johnson Space Center on October 15 for the crew to discuss the flight.
why_it_matters: Long station flights build skills and science needed for future Moon and Mars trips. Safe crew returns also show how complex teamwork on Earth supports exploration.
